work_item: Isolated scene background and foreground with an unchanged usable peer

source.reason: Approved scene-local background/restart and focus semantics
Scene-keyed suspension/resume is idempotent and addresses only its stack
Existing deterministic scene-scoped lifecycle controls; not rerun or treated as physical proof
Serial activation alternates peer backgrounding and has separate failed disconnect
Latest observed scene state has no H10 armed-cycle identity
Complete owner-bound lifecycle journal and fresh native scene/window/input inventory
Native scene presentation witness and generic versus scene-context marker paths
Unscoped marker attributes do not select an owner; raw independent mapper and lifecycle capture
Probe deployment target27.0; existing SDK deployment15 compatibility unchanged

contract: Background only A, then restore A, while B remains in the foreground and its current RUM view occurrence stays unchanged. Losing focus while visible is permitted. A ends its original view and returns with a fresh occurrence.
preserve: H04 final reviewed plan/product and original EXP196 invalid disconnect remain unchanged.
H06 original719 source inputs and signed product remain unchanged.
Existing source, lifetime and compatibility evidence remains accepted; no rerun or simulator substitution.
S2 prepared SwiftUI sessions await fresh human readiness after September30 09:00 Paris.

findings.fact: H04 deliberately backgrounds the peer at every activation; it cannot prove uninterrupted B ownership across A background/foreground.
findings.action: Use a separately named one-cycle fixture with both scenes foreground before the critical interval.

findings.fact: emitLifecycleMarker adds source attributes but sends unscoped work. After A returns, generic work intended for B could follow the process representative.
findings.action: Use fresh scene resolution for each marker, with existing DEBUG scene-context dispatch or reviewed explicit scene target; source tags never count as owner proof. Do not reuse a captured view target that could hide a replaced current view.

findings.fact: A latest recorded scene-state value does not identify a background/foreground cycle after this admission.
findings.action: Freeze original owners and lifecycle-journal revision at the armed barrier; require fresh actual A notifications and owner-bound state after that revision. No synthetic notifications or consumed old readiness.

scenario.tracking: Existing manual trackRUMView on identical Home content in two scenes; no navigation or public API expansion.
scenario.environment: Physical iPad on iOS27 in an already authorized windowing mode that preserves usable B while A is minimized/restored. Physical Duo remains separate.

phases.state: A and B foreground-active or foreground-inactive, connected with exact original native owners. Actual display shows both fixture windows.
phases.owners: Capture the independently mapped current A and B occurrences after setup; do not require absolute occurrence1 or count setup reactivations as failures.

phases.input: Minimize only A using the actual OS window control.
phases.state: Fresh actual A didEnterBackground after the armed journal revision; A background is required. B stays foreground-active or foreground-inactive. At every marker B must retain the same connected scene/window/controller/generation, visible mounted content, enabled window/root interaction, attached enabled reliable input observer with zero active touches, and no active transition/resize. If B is foreground-active its fixture window must own its scene key window. Actual display identifies B as visible and unobstructed.
phases.owners: A original view ends; B marker retains its captured current view ID.

phases.input: Restore A beside B using the actual OS window control.
phases.state: Fresh actual A willEnterForeground and settled foreground state after its background, same native owner identities; B remains foreground. Actual display shows both windows.
phases.owners: A marker uses one fresh occurrence distinct from its original; B marker keeps its original occurrence.

scope_limits: One A cycle, five Action/Resource pairs, three critical view occurrences. Complete setup and tail inventories are retained separately.
No disconnect/remount, close-window, restoration, H06 Operation, interactive navigation, performance or physical-Duo credit.
No repeated SDK-on/off diagnosis; if the chosen OS action fails its expected effect, preserve evidence and stop that path.

native: Freeze distinct logical/native scene, scene object, window, controller, generation and input-observer identities before the critical interval.
Keep an append-only complete lifecycle journal and inventory of all actual windows, including auxiliary windows; no window-count or private-class-name rule.

Accept expected focus/key and geometry changes, including B foreground-inactive at a marker under the explicit usable-owner predicate. Reject B background/disconnect/owner replacement, whole-application background, journal gaps, or unsupported input. A background is the intended middle phase, not an invalidation.

Observe each transition before its work. Returned native observations are retained verbatim; no substitution from a prior capture. Actual display anchors qualify topology, not sidebar icons or local frame coordinates alone.

Freeze armRevision in the copied fixture after both original foreground owners qualify. Require an owner-bound A didEnterBackground with revision greater than armRevision, followed by an owner-bound A willEnterForeground with a greater revision. Each settled-state witness must include the corresponding journal prefix before work. Never satisfy these boundaries with the generic latest-state signal alone.

B focus activation/deactivation, key-window changes, layout changes and ordinary RUM document-version updates are allowed. The forbidden changes are B becoming background/disconnected, replacement of a native owner, or ending/replacing its current RUM occurrence. No blanket ban on B lifecycle or view-document revisions.
rum: Join independent mapper View, Action and Resource identities to each exact marker and native scene. Source attributes alone never establish ownership.
Capture current A/B occurrences after setup and before the requested cycle. Allow earlier legitimate setup occurrences but inventory every one.
Require original A stop plus one new A view after return; B keeps its current ID and never ends/restarts during the critical interval. All critical work uses one RUM session.
Require exactly five uniquely identified Action/Resource pairs at the selected current owners; reject missing, duplicate, aliased, unexpected or cross-scene work and errors/crashes.
Use event attribution and document revisions, not mapper serialization order against synchronous UI callbacks or strict timing/float equality.
evidence: Keep scenario, local/backend evidence and cleanup verdicts separate. Build/oracle PASS is preparation only.
Use complete paginated session inventory with exact event/owner joins; delayed upload is pending evidence and never a reason to repeat gestures.
Bind helper/source/compiler/all-MachO/run/process identity and a fresh one-cell admission before any launch.
Require safe release/native-idle and worker quiescence before task-only cleanup; preserve original failures and separate restorations.

offline_negative_controls: Stale pre-arm A background/foreground accepted as the cycle
Transient B background followed by foreground
A reuses its old RUM occurrence or produces extra new occurrences
B stops/restarts even with the same view name
B marker follows A process representative
Missing/duplicate work or incomplete backend inventory
Setup occurrences or asynchronously serialized mapper rows incorrectly classified as extra critical views
Auxiliary windows and harmless floating-point geometry changes incorrectly rejected
Late native/display evidence or dropped lifecycle journal rows

oracle_component.scope: Offline component only; complete sealed source-bound transfer, typed native producer, display, composed runner and cleanup remain separate.
